# Template: tutorial

**Reusable template, not a runnable tutorial.** Replace these instructions with a finished tutorial and supply complete example files. Follow the [documentation standard](../contributing/documentation-standard.md).

## What you will build

Describe a small useful result and what the reader will learn. Distinguish configuration checks from target operations. Name the complete synthetic source files and compatible dependencies.

## Prepare the environment

Specify the initial working directory and every tool. Give complete commands to prepare an isolated environment with hash-locked dependencies. Use YAML for site and definition files; explain any required fixed JSON indexes or runtime JSON. Resolve symlinks in temporary source roots, and place reports in new child paths that do not yet exist.

## Author and understand the configuration

Show minimal valid YAML and explain the chosen values, defaults and references. Include or link all required contexts, profiles, software, networks, policies and secret-source metadata. Do not assume unexplained “existing” prerequisites.

## Run and inspect

Give complete commands from explicit working directories, describe the expected output and show how to inspect the generated result safely. Explain that private deployment packets must stay private.

## Make a practical change

Change one value, predict its effect, rerun validation and compare the results. Add a meaningful invalid variation and explain the expected failure.

## First installation and later deployments

State whether the tutorial is offline-only or has been tested for installation on a target. For supported installation, explain fresh creation, evidence of HomeLab ownership and later updates without changing lifecycle. Link to the selected profile's limits.

## Check your result and continue

Name the maintained compiler or example test and explain what it establishes. State known limits, give cleanup steps only for disposable resources created by the tutorial, and link to the next guides. Replace every placeholder so the tutorial ends with a reproducible result.

## Author review before publication

Connect named examples to complete canonical files and the existing parser, validator and compiler tests. Record compatible source selections, evidence obtained and any hosted or target checks not performed. Follow the [assurance guide](../contributing/documentation-assurance.md), check local link destinations and read the full rendered tutorial. Use ordinary verbs, name who performs each action and explain project-specific terms at first use. Preserve exact requirements and evidence limits. Remove all authoring instructions and placeholders before publication.
